cbv29b:17.1.verse: Whoever, dear Sir - be they monk or nun

cbv29b:17.2.verse: or layman or laywoman - learns this “Āṭānāṭiya” protection well,

cbv29b:17.3.verse: and will master it in its entirety, then if a non-human being -

cbv29b:17.4.verse: be they male yakkha or female yakkha or yakkha boy

cbv29b:17.5.verse: or yakkha girl or yakkha minister

cbv29b:17.6.verse: or yakkha councillor or yakkha messenger

cbv29b:17.7.verse: or male gandhabba or female gandhabba or gandhabba boy

cbv29b:17.8.verse: or gandhabba girl or gandhabba minister

cbv29b:17.9.verse: or gandhabba councillor or gandhabba messenger

cbv29b:17.10.verse: or male kumbhaṇḍa or female kumbhaṇḍa or kumbhaṇḍa boy

cbv29b:17.11.verse: or kumbhaṇḍa girl or kumbhaṇḍa minister

cbv29b:17.12.verse: or kumbhaṇḍa councillor or kumbhaṇḍa messenger

cbv29b:17.13.verse: or male nāga or female nāga or nāga boy

cbv29b:17.14.verse: or nāga girl or nāga minister

cbv29b:17.15.verse: or nāga councillor or nāga messenger -

cbv29b:17.16.verse: with a wicked mind should come near while they are going, or stand near while they are standing,

cbv29b:17.17.verse: or sit near while they are sitting, or lie near while they are lying,

cbv29b:18.1.1.verse: then that non-human being, dear Sir, would not receive in my villages and towns, honour or respect.

cbv29b:18.1.2.verse: That non-human being, dear Sir, would not receive in my royal city Ālakamandā, ground or dwelling.

cbv29b:18.1.3.verse: That non-human being, dear Sir, would not be able to go to the gathering of the yakkhas.

cbv29b:18.1.4.verse: Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would not give or take him in marriage.

cbv29b:18.1.5.verse: Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would abuse him with very personal abuse.

cbv29b:18.1.6.verse: Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would drop an empty bowl over his head.

cbv29b:18.1.7.verse: Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would split his head into seven pieces.

cbv29b:18.1.8.verse: There are non-human beings, dear Sir, who are fierce, cruel, and violent, they do not take notice of the Great Kings, they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ men, they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ mens’ men,

cbv29b:18.1.9.verse: and those non-human beings, dear Sir, are said to be in revolt against the Great Kings.

cbv29b:18.1.10.verse: Just as, dear Sir, there are thieves in the king of Magadha’s realm,

cbv29b:18.1.11.verse: who do not take notice of the king of Magadha, who do not take notice of the king of Magadha’s men, who do not take notice of the king of Magadha’s mens’ men,

cbv29b:18.1.12.verse: and those great thieves, dear Sir, are said to be in revolt against the king of Magadha.

cbv29b:18.1.13.verse: Even so, dear Sir, there are non-human beings who are fierce, cruel, and violent, they do not take notice of the Great Kings, they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ men, they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ mens’ men,

cbv29b:18.1.14.verse: and those non-human beings, dear Sir, are said to be in revolt against the Great Kings.

cbv29b:19.1.verse: Now, dear Sir, whatever non-human beings -

cbv29b:19.2.verse: be they male yakkha or female yakkha or yakkha boy

cbv29b:19.3.verse: or yakkha girl or yakkha minister

cbv29b:19.4.verse: or yakkha councillor or yakkha messenger

cbv29b:19.5.verse: or male gandhabba or female gandhabba or gandhabba boy

cbv29b:19.6.verse: or gandhabba girl or gandhabba minister

cbv29b:19.7.verse: or gandhabba councillor or gandhabba messenger

cbv29b:19.8.verse: or male kumbhaṇḍa or female kumbhaṇḍa or kumbhaṇḍa boy

cbv29b:19.9.verse: or kumbhaṇḍa girl or kumbhaṇḍa minister

cbv29b:19.10.verse: or kumbhaṇḍa councillor or kumbhaṇḍa messenger

cbv29b:19.11.verse: or male nāga or female nāga or nāga boy

cbv29b:19.12.verse: or nāga girl or nāga minister

cbv29b:19.13.verse: or nāga councillor or nāga messenger -

cbv29b:19.14.verse: with a wicked mind should come near a monk or a nun or a layman or a laywoman

cbv29b:19.15.verse: while they are going, or stand near while they are standing,

cbv29b:19.16.verse: or sit near while they are sitting, or lie near while they are lying,

cbv29b:20.1.1.verse: then to these yakkhas, great yakkhas, generals, great generals, one should call out, one should shout out, one should cry out:

cbv29b:20.1.2.verse: “This yakkha has seized me, this yakkha has grabbed me, this yakkha annoys me, this yakkha harasses me, this yakkha hurts me, this yakkha injures me, this yakkha will not release me.”

cbv29b:20.1.3.verse: To which yakkhas, great yakkhas, generals, and great generals?

cbv29b:20.1.22.verse: then to these yakkhas, great yakkhas, generals, and great generals, one should call out, one should shout out, one should cry out:

cbv29b:20.1.23.verse: “This yakkha has seized me, this yakkha has grabbed me, this yakkha annoys me, this yakkha harasses me, this yakkha hurts me, this yakkha injures me, this yakkha will not release me.”

cbv29b:20.1.24.verse: This, dear Sir, is the “Āṭānāṭiyā” protection, for the monks’, nuns’, laymen’s, and laywomen’s guard, protection, freedom from harm, and comfortable living.

cbv29b:20.1.25.verse: And now, dear Sir, we shall go, as we have many duties, and there is much which ought to be done.”

cbv29b:20.1.26.verse: “Now is the time for whatever you Great Kings are thinking.”

cbv29b:20.1.27.verse: Then the Four Great Kings, monks, rose from their seats and after worshipping and circumambulating me, vanished right there.

cbv29b:20.1.28.verse: Then some yakkhas, monks, rose from their seats and after worshipping and circumambulating me, vanished right there.

cbv29b:20.1.29.verse: Some exchanged greetings with me, and after exchanging polite and courteous greetings, vanished right there.

cbv29b:20.1.30.verse: Some, after raising their hands in respectful salutation to me, vanished right there.

cbv29b:20.1.31.verse: Some, after announcing their name and family vanished right there.

cbv29b:20.1.32.verse: And some, while keeping silent, vanished right there.

cbv29b:20.1.35.verse: bear in mind the “Āṭānāṭiya” protection, monks,

cbv29b:20.1.36.verse: the “Āṭānāṭiya” protection, monks, is for your welfare and benefit, for the monks’, nuns’, laymen’s, and laywomen’s guard, protection, freedom from harm, and comfortable living.”

cbv29b:20.1.38.verse: and those monks were uplifted and greatly rejoiced in what was said by the Fortunate One.

cbv29b:22.1.verse: By this declaration of the truth may you be safe at all times!

cbv29b:22.2.verse: By this declaration of the truth may you have the blessing of success!

cbv29b:22.3.verse: By this declaration of the truth may all disease be destroyed!

cbv29b:24.1.verse: The Text of the Four Recitals is Finished

cbv29b:2.1.1.verse: Then, when the night had passed, the Buddha told the mendicants all that had happened, repeating all the verses spoken. Then he added:

cbv29b:20.1.36.verse: The Āṭānāṭiya protection is beneficial, and is for the guarding, protection, safety, and comfort of the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen.”

cbv29b:20.1.37.verse: That is what the Buddha said.

cbv29b:20.1.38.verse: Satisfied, the mendicants approved what the Buddha said.

mp5:1.1.25.verse: Even as a mother would protect with her life

mp5:1.1.29.verse: With love for the whole world,

mp5:1.1.34.verse: or lying down while yet unweary,

mp5:1.1.36.verse: for this, they say, is a divine meditation in this life.

mp5:1.1.39.verse: with desire for sensual pleasures dispelled,

mp5:1.1.40.verse: they never return to a womb again.

mp6:2.1.verse: Whatever bad sign, inauspicious event, or whatever ominous bird shriek there is,

mp6:2.2.verse: also evil planets, and unpleasant dreams may they perish through the power of the Buddha!

mp6:3.1.verse: Whatever bad sign, inauspicious event, or whatever ominous bird shriek there is,

mp6:3.2.verse: also evil planets, and unpleasant dreams may they perish through the power of the Dhamma!

mp6:4.1.verse: whatever bad sign, inauspicious event, or whatever ominous bird shriek there is,

mp6:4.2.verse: also evil planets, and unpleasant dreams may they perish through the power of the Saṅgha!

mp6:6.1.verse: May those who suffer be without suffering, may those who fear be without fear,

mp6:6.2.verse: may those who grieve be without grief - may all living creatures be so!

mp6:7.1.verse: All the Buddhas’ strength, and whatever strength the Independent Buddhas

mp6:7.2.verse: and Worthy Ones have, by that power we bind this protection in every way!

mp6:8.1.verse: May there be every blessing, and may all of the gods protect you,

mp6:8.2.verse: by the power of all the Buddhas may you be safe forever!

mp6:9.1.verse: May there be every blessing, and may all of the gods protect you,

mp6:9.2.verse: by the power of all that is Dhamma may you be safe forever!

mp6:10.1.verse: May there be every blessing, and may all of the gods protect you,

mp6:10.2.verse: by the power of the whole Saṅgha may you be safe forever!

mp6:11.1.verse: ° Warding off all unlucky stars, yakkhas, bhūtas, and evil planets,

mp6:11.2.verse: by the power of this safeguard may all their adversities end!

mp6:12.1.verse: Reverence to him, the Fortunate One, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha

upg1:0.2.verse: Verses on the Blessings of Success

upg1:1.1.verse: ° Māra, the terrible one, who had created a thousand arms with weapons,

upg1:1.2.verse: and had mounted on (the elephant) Girimekhala, with his army,

upg1:1.3.verse: did the lord of sages defeat by such things as generosity and so forth -

upg1:1.4.verse: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!

upg1:2.1.verse: ° Even more terrible than Māra was the impatient and obdurate yakkha Ālavaka,

upg1:2.2.verse: who fought (with the Buddha) throughout the whole night,

upg1:2.3.verse: (him) did the lord of sages defeat by his patience and self-control

upg1:2.4.verse: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!

upg1:3.1.verse: The great elephant Nālāgiri, who was completely intoxicated,

upg1:3.2.verse: fearful, like a jungle fire, a flaming discus, or a flash of lightning,

upg1:3.3.verse: did the lord of sages defeat by sprinkling (him) with the waters of friendliness -

upg1:3.4.verse: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!

upg1:4.1.verse: With a sword that was lifted high in his outstretched hand, that very fearsome (bandit)

upg1:4.2.verse: the one with a finger necklace (Aṅgulimāla) ran for (the whole of) three leagues up the path:

upg1:4.3.verse: (him) did the lord of sages defeat with the psychic powers created in his mind -

upg1:4.4.verse: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!

upg1:5.1.verse: Having made her midriff (look large) with a piece of wood, like one who is pregnant,

upg1:5.2.verse: Ciñcā (then spoke) wicked words in the midst of a group of people:

upg1:5.3.verse: (her) did the lord of sages defeat by means of his gentleness and peacefulness -

upg1:5.4.verse: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!

upg1:6.1.verse: The arrogant Saccaka, who had given up the truth, and had challenged (the Buddha) to a debate,

upg1:6.2.verse: with his mind fixed on his argument, completely blind to the truth,

upg1:6.3.verse: (him) did the lord of sages defeat with the shining lamp of true wisdom -

upg1:6.4.verse: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!

upg1:7.1.verse: ° Taming the wise dragon Nandopananda, who had great power,

upg1:7.2.verse: by way of his son (Moggallāna), who was a dragon of an elder,

upg1:7.3.verse: (thus) did the lord of sages defeat (him) by instructing (his son to use) psychic power -

upg1:7.4.verse: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!

upg1:8.1.verse: He whose hand was badly bitten by the serpent of wrongly taken up views,

upg1:8.2.verse: the brahma Baka, who was clear and bright, and who possessed psychic powers,

upg1:8.3.verse: did the lord of sages defeat with the medicine of his super-knowledge -

upg1:8.4.verse: through that resplendent power may you have the blessings of success!

upg1:9.1.verse: ° He who recites these eight verses each and every day,

upg1:9.2.verse: which are about the Buddha’s (many) blessed successes, and remembers them with diligence,

upg1:9.3.verse: after giving up (all) the many and various kinds of adversity,

upg1:9.4.verse: that wise man will (soon thereafter) attain both freedom and happiness.

upg2:0.1.verse: The Verses on the Great Blessings of Success

upg2:1.1.verse: The lord of great compassion, for the benefit of all living creatures,

upg2:1.2.verse: having fulfilled all the perfections has attained supreme and Complete Awakening.

upg2:1.3.verse: By this declaration of the truth may you have the blessing of success!

upg2:2.1.verse: Succeeding at the root of the Bodhi tree he furthered the Sakyans’ joy -

upg2:2.2.verse: so may you be successful, may you succeed with the blessing of success!

upg2:3.1.verse: Having honoured the Buddha treasure, the best and supreme medicine,

upg2:3.2.verse: of benefit to gods and men, by the blessed power of the Buddha

upg2:3.3.verse: may all adversities perish, and all suffering come to an end for you!

upg2:4.1.verse: Having honoured the Dhamma treasure, the best and supreme medicine,

upg2:4.2.verse: which brings fevers to an end, by the blessed power of the Dhamma

upg2:4.3.verse: may all adversities perish, and all fear come to an end for you!

upg2:5.1.verse: Having honoured the Saṅgha treasure, the best and supreme medicine,

upg2:5.2.verse: worthy of gifts and hospitality, by the blessed power of the Saṅgha

upg2:5.3.verse: may all adversities perish, and all disease come to an end for you!

upg2:6.1.verse: Whatever the many and various treasures there are in the world

upg2:6.2.verse: no treasure is equal to the Buddha: through this (truth) may you be safe!

upg2:7.1.verse: Whatever the many and various treasures there are in the world

upg2:7.2.verse: no treasure is equal to the Dhamma: through this (truth) may you be safe!

upg2:8.1.verse: Whatever the many and various treasures there are in the world

upg2:8.2.verse: no treasure is equal to the Saṅgha: through this (truth) may you be safe!

upg2:9.1.verse: For me there is no other refuge, for me the Buddha is the best refuge!

upg2:9.2.verse: By this declaration of the truth may you have the blessing of success!

upg2:10.1.verse: For me there is no other refuge, for me the Dhamma is the best refuge!

upg2:10.2.verse: By this declaration of the truth may you have the blessing of success!

upg2:11.1.verse: For me there is no other refuge, for me the Saṅgha is the best refuge!

upg2:11.2.verse: By this declaration of the truth may you have the blessing of success!

upg2:12.1.verse: May you avoid all calamities and may all disease be destroyed,

upg2:12.2.verse: may there be no obstacles for you, may you be happy and live long!

upg3:1.1.verse: Those (gods) who are peaceful, with peaceful minds, who have taken refuge in the triple refuge, whether here, or above the worlds,

upg3:1.2.verse: the various earth gods, that group who have taken up, and are engaged in, virtuous deeds all of the time,

upg3:1.3.verse: may these gods come, those who dwell on the majestic Mt. Meru, that excellent golden mountain,

upg3:1.4.verse: peacefully, and with good reason, ( to hear) the Sage’s excellent word about entering the stream, and harmony.

upg3:2.1.verse: May all yakkhas, gods, and deities, from the whole universe,

upg3:2.2.verse: ° after partaking of the merits, and of all the thoroughly good fortune

upg3:2.3.verse: we have acquired, being in harmony, and delighting in the teaching,

upg3:2.4.verse: be not heedless and grant us complete protection.

upg3:3.1.verse: May the teaching and the world be on the increase every day,

upg3:3.2.verse: And may the gods every day protect the teaching and the world.

upg3:4.1.verse: ° May you, and all those who are around you, together with

upg3:4.2.verse: all your relatives, be untroubled, happy, and easy in mind.

upg3:5.1.verse: (may you be protected) from the king, thieves, humans, and non-humans,

upg3:5.2.verse: from fire and water, demons, stumps, and thorns,

upg3:5.4.verse: from what is not the true dhamma, not right view, not a good person,

upg3:5.5.verse: and from fierce elephants, horses, antelopes, bulls, dogs, snakes, scorpions, poisonous serpents,

upg3:5.6.verse: panthers, bears, hyenas, wild boars, buffaloes, yakkhas, rakkhasas, and so on,

upg3:5.7.verse: from the manifold fears, the manifold diseases,

upg3:5.8.verse: the manifold calamities, (from all of these troubles) may you receive protection!

upg3:6.1.verse: Beginning with the aspiration (for Buddhahood, and thinking of) the Realised One’s ten perfections,

upg3:6.2.verse: ten minor perfections, ten great perfections - altogether thirty perfections,

upg3:6.3.verse: his five great sacrifices, three ways of conduct,

upg3:6.4.verse: descent into the womb for his final existence, birth,

upg3:6.5.verse: Great Renunciation, life of effort, sitting cross legged at the Bodhi tree, victory over Māra,

upg3:6.6.verse: his penetration and knowledge of omniscience, and his nine supermundane attainments,

upg3:6.7.verse: and after considering all these Buddha qualities, (going around) the three walls of Vesāli,

upg3:6.8.verse: during the three watches of the night, the venerable elder Ānanda,

upg3:6.9.verse: after establishing great compassion in his heart, made this safeguard.

upg4:1.1.verse: Those heroes, sat on their thrones, after defeating Māra and his host,

upg4:1.2.verse: those who are bulls of men, drank of the ambrosia of the four truths.

upg4:2.1.verse: Those twenty eight leaders, Buddhas, beginning with Taṇhaṅkara,

upg4:2.2.verse: are all established on the crown of your head, they are lords of sages.

upg4:3.1.verse: The Buddhas are established on your head, and the Dhamma on your eyes,

upg4:3.2.verse: the Saṅgha, the fount of all good qualities is established on your chest,

upg4:4.1.verse: On your heart is Anuruddha, and Sāriputta on your right,

upg4:4.2.verse: Koṇḍañña is on your back, and Moggallāna on your left.

upg4:5.1.verse: On your right ear (are established these two) Ānanda and Rāhula,

upg4:5.2.verse: Kassapa and Mahānāma, these two (are established) on your left ear.

upg4:6.1.verse: At the end of your hair at the back like the sun, the light maker -

upg4:6.2.verse: is seated the glorious Sobhita, who is a bull of a sage.

upg4:7.1.verse: The one named Kumārakassapa, great sage, and beautiful speaker,

upg4:7.2.verse: that fount of good qualities is permanently established on your mouth.

upg4:8.1.verse: Puṇṇa, Aṅgulimāla, Upāli, Nanda, and Sivalī -

upg4:8.2.verse: these five true elders (are established like) auspicious signs on your forehead.

upg4:9.1.verse: The remaining eighty great elders, victors, disciples of the victor,

upg4:9.2.verse: shining with the power of virtue, are established on your limbs.

upg4:10.1.verse: To the front is “The Treasures” on the right “The Friendliness Discourse”,

upg4:10.2.verse: “The Banner” is at the back, and “Aṅgulimāla” is on the left,

upg4:11.1.verse: The “Constituent Groups” and “Peacock” safeguards, and the “Āṭānāṭiya Discourse”,

upg4:11.2.verse: cover the space (around you), the remainder are a fence, so to speak.

upg4:12.1.verse: With the strength of the victor’s order, equipped with the fence of the Dhamma,

upg4:12.2.verse: engaged in the four duties, in the Sambuddhas’ armour forever,

upg4:13.1.verse: may all internal and external adversities that arise, beginning with wind and bile,

upg4:13.2.verse: through the power of (the Buddhas’) endless virtues, come to a complete end.

upg4:14.1.verse: While living on this great earth, standing in the midst of the victors’ armour,

upg4:14.2.verse: may all of those great bulls of men watch over you forever.

upg4:15.1.verse: Thus being continuously well protected, with adversity defeated through the victors’ power,

upg4:15.2.verse: with the crowd of foes destroyed through the Buddhas’ power, live on, guarded by the power of the true Dhamma!

upg4:16.1.verse: Thus being continuously well protected, with adversity defeated through the victors’ power,

upg4:16.2.verse: with the crowd of foes destroyed through the Dhamma’s power, live on, guarded by the power of the true Dhamma!

upg4:17.1.verse: Thus being continuously well protected, with adversity defeated through the victors’ power,

upg4:17.2.verse: with the crowd of foes destroyed through the Saṅgha’s power, live on, guarded by the power of the true Dhamma!

upg4:18.1.verse: You are defended by the fence of the true Dhamma, with the eight noble ones in the eight directions,

upg4:18.2.verse: and in between these (directions) are the eight lords, and above, like a canopy, stand the victors.

upg4:19.1.verse: Breaking Māra’s army, the Teacher who sat under the Bodhi tree now rests on your head.

upg4:19.2.verse: You have Moggallāna dwelling on your left hand side, and Sāriputta on your right.

upg4:19.3.verse: ° The Dhamma dwells in the middle of your chest, the Awakening One who took birth from

upg4:19.4.verse: out of a peahen’s womb has come to your feet, he is brilliant, the world’s sole protector.

upg4:20.1.verse: All inauspicious events, adversities, and bad signs,

upg4:20.2.verse: all calamities, diseases, blame, bad planets, bar none,

upg4:20.3.verse: all obstacles, fears, and unpleasant dreams -

upg4:20.4.verse: may (all of them), through the excellent power of the Buddha, go to destruction!

upg4:21.1.verse: All inauspicious events, adversities, and bad signs,

upg4:21.2.verse: all calamities, diseases, blame, bad planets, bar none,

upg4:21.3.verse: all obstacles, fears, and unpleasant dreams -

upg4:21.4.verse: may (all of them), through the excellent power of the Dhamma, go to destruction!

upg4:22.1.verse: All inauspicious events, adversities, and bad signs,

upg4:22.2.verse: all calamities, diseases, blame, bad planets, bar none,

upg4:22.3.verse: all obstacles, fears, and unpleasant dreams -

upg4:22.4.verse: may (all of them), through the excellent power of the Saṅgha, go to destruction!

upg5:1.1.verse: Taṇhaṅkara, the great hero, Medhaṅkara, of great repute,

upg5:1.2.verse: Saraṇaṅkara, who benefits the world, Dīpaṅkara, the bright one,

upg5:2.1.verse: Koṇḍañña, head of the people, Maṅgala, a bull of a man,

upg5:2.2.verse: The wise one Sumana, whose mind is well, Revata, who increases delight,

upg5:3.1.verse: Sobhita, endowed with good qualities, Anomadassī, supreme man,

upg5:3.2.verse: Paduma, the lamp of the world, Nārada, the best of guides,

upg5:4.1.verse: Padumuttara, an excellent being, Sumedha, the greatest person,

upg5:4.2.verse: Sujāta, greatest in all the world, Piyadassī, a bull of a man,

upg5:5.1.verse: Atthadassī, the compassionate one, Dhammadassī, darkness-dispeller,

upg5:5.2.verse: Siddhattha, unequalled in the world, Tissa, who was most restrained,

upg5:6.1.verse: Phussa, excellent Sambuddha, Vipassī, who has no likeness,

upg5:6.2.verse: Sikhī, the Teacher who is a benefit to all, Vessabhū, who gives happiness,

upg5:7.1.verse: Kakusandha, the leader of the pack, Koṇāgamana, who gave up what is harmful,

upg5:7.2.verse: Kassapa, the glorious one, and Gotama, the Sakyan bull.

upg5:8.1.verse: Through their truth and virtue, and the strength of their patience and friendliness,

upg5:8.2.verse: may these (Buddhas) always protect you with good health and happiness!

upg6:1.1.verse: Recollection of the Buddha, friendliness, unattractiveness, and mindfulness of death -

upg6:1.2.verse: these are the four protective meditations that a virtuous monk should develop.

upg6:2.1.verse: Recollecting the Sage’s virtue, and his endless, extensive, good qualities,

upg6:2.2.verse: the wise monk should develop the recollection of the Buddha first.

upg6:4.1.verse: Alone he destroyed all the corruptions, and (bad) predispositions,

upg6:4.2.verse: and being continually and fully pure he is worthy of worship at all times.

upg6:5.1.verse: ° The Sage by himself has, in every way, completely awakened to all things

upg6:5.2.verse: throughout the whole of time, and alone he has arrived at omniscience.

upg6:6.1.verse: ° Being endowed with great psychic power, good conduct, virtue, and so on,

upg6:6.2.verse: true understanding, insight, and so on, the leader was like the shining sky.

upg6:7.1.verse: He who never spoke foolish words, has arrived at that glorious state (Nibbāna),

upg6:7.2.verse: he knew the threefold world system (completely) without leaving anything out.

upg6:8.1.verse: Overflowing with countless good qualities he is supreme among all beings,

upg6:8.2.verse: with countless skilful means he tamed those men who could be tamed.

upg6:9.1.verse: He alone, to the whole world was the teacher of everything good,

upg6:9.2.verse: he is the highest treasure, having qualities such as good fortune, mastery, and so on.

upg6:10.1.verse: Being wise in regard to all things compassionate to everybody,

upg6:10.2.verse: he exceeded (others) in the best qualities, (knowing) what was for his own and others’ good.

upg6:11.1.verse: Through sympathy he set his mind on the perfections through wisdom he raised himself up,

upg6:11.2.verse: he raised himself above all things, through sympathy he raised others too.

upg6:12.1.verse: Even his visible form-body was beyond thought,

upg6:12.2.verse: what can be said of his spiritual body, which was unique, having powerful knowledge?

upg6:14.1.verse: In a similar way to oneself, all beings desire happiness,

upg6:14.2.verse: having seen that one should gradually develop friendliness towards all beings.

upg6:15.1.verse: May I constantly be happy, free from suffering, and like myself

upg6:15.2.verse: may my benefactors be happy, neutral persons, and foes also.

upg6:16.1.verse: In this village, and its surrounding fields, may beings always be happy,

upg6:16.2.verse: and those in other countries, and people throughout the universe.

upg6:17.1.verse: ° Throughout the entire universe may the countless beings, creatures,

upg6:17.2.verse: persons, and bhūtas, who have attained individuality, be happy,

upg6:18.1.verse: and so too (all) women, men, noble ones, and also ignoble ones,

upg6:18.2.verse: gods, humans, and fallen creatures, and likewise (all beings) in the ten directions.

upg6:20.1.verse: With consciousness it is unattractive, just as it is without (i.e. dead),

upg6:20.2.verse: seeing this body as unattractive, a monk should develop (the recollection) of the unattractive.

upg6:21.1.verse: Thus by way of colour, shape, smell, location, and appearance,

upg6:21.2.verse: the thirty-two (parts) in my body (are like) repulsive corpses.

upg6:22.1.verse: The (parts) that depend on this body are contemptible, as is what falls from a corpse,

upg6:22.2.verse: for their receptacle is impure, they are situated in this corpse of a body.

upg6:23.1.verse: Like a worm in excrement this body arose in what is impure (i.e. the womb),

upg6:23.2.verse: inside it is full of impurities just like a full lavatory.

upg6:24.1.verse: Always the impurities overflow like fat (overflows) from a frying pan,

upg6:24.2.verse: various kinds of worms dwell in it, the same as in a cesspool.

upg6:25.1.verse: This bodily heap is like a boil, like a disease, or like a sore,

upg6:25.2.verse: it is incurable, contemptible, just like a rotting corpse.

upg6:27.1.verse: By comparing a lamp in a breeze, with the destruction of the life continuum,

upg6:27.2.verse: through seeing oneself as similar to others, one should develop mindfulness of death.

upg6:28.1.verse: Just as people who have attained great good fortune here have died,

upg6:28.2.verse: in the same way will I die death is (surely) coming to me.

upg6:29.1.verse: Indeed death always comes along with that which has arisen,

upg6:29.2.verse: it is like a murderer who is seeking an opportunity to kill.

upg6:30.1.verse: ° This life is slowly, without turning back, continually, eagerly,

upg6:30.2.verse: going its way, it rises and falls just as the sun runs its course (and sets).

upg6:31.1.verse: (Like) lightning, a bubble, dew, a line drawn on water, life (quickly goes to) destruction,

upg6:31.2.verse: like an executioner in regard to his rival (death) can never be constrained.

upg6:32.1.verse: Even the two kinds of Victors, who are famous, strong, meritorious, powerful, and of great intelligence,

upg6:32.2.verse: were quickly slaughtered by death, so what to say about one like me?

upg6:33.1.verse: When conditions fail there are internal and external adversities,

upg6:33.2.verse: dying at each and every moment I will die in less (time) than a blink of an eye.

upg6:35.1.verse: Having developed these four protections one should consider next

upg6:35.2.verse: the eight great bases for urgency, having non-stop energy.

upg6:36.1.verse: Birth, old age, sickness, death, the lower realms,

upg6:36.2.verse: the past and future suffering in the round,

upg6:36.3.verse: the suffering in having to seek food in the present -

upg6:36.4.verse: these are the eight bases for urgency.

upg6:37.1.verse: If, in the morning and in the evening, one who knows the way,

upg6:37.2.verse: who desires his own benefit, practises (these meditations) continually,

upg6:37.3.verse: ° then after destroying (even) extensive obstacles, that sage

upg6:37.4.verse: easily attains great happiness, and the distinction of the deathless.

upg7:1.1.verse: May all creatures, all breathing creatures, all beings,

upg7:1.4.verse: all those who are Noble, all those who are not (yet) Noble,

upg7:1.5.verse: all gods, all human beings, all who have fallen (into the lower worlds),

upg7:1.6.verse: be free from hatred, free from oppression, free from trouble,

upg7:1.7.verse: may they take care of themselves and be happy, may they be free from suffering,

upg7:1.8.verse: being ones who own their actions, may they not lose whatever prosperity they have gained.

upg7:2.1.verse: In the Eastern direction, in the Western direction,

upg7:2.2.verse: in the Northern direction, in the Southern direction,

upg7:2.3.verse: in the South-Eastern direction, in the North-West direction,

upg7:2.4.verse: in the North-East direction, in the South-West direction,

upg7:2.5.verse: in the lower direction, in the upper direction.

upg7:3.1.verse: May all creatures, all breathing creatures, all beings,

upg7:3.4.verse: all those who are Noble, all those who are not (yet) Noble,

upg7:3.5.verse: all gods, all human beings, all who have fallen (into the lower worlds),

upg7:3.6.verse: be free from hatred, free from oppression, free from trouble,

upg7:3.7.verse: may they take care of themselves and be happy, may they be free from suffering,

upg7:3.8.verse: being ones who own their actions, may they not lose whatever prosperity they have gained.

upg7:4.1.verse: From the top of existence down, and from the Avīci hell up,

upg7:4.2.verse: everywhere in the universe, whatever beings live on the earth,

upg7:4.3.verse: (may they be) free from oppression, free from hatred, free from suffering, and free from danger.

upg7:5.1.verse: From the top of existence down, and from the Avīci hell up,

upg7:5.2.verse: everywhere in the universe, whatever beings live in the water,

upg7:5.3.verse: (may they be) free from oppression, free from hatred, free from suffering, and free from danger.

upg7:6.1.verse: From the top of existence down, and from the Avīci hell up,

upg7:6.2.verse: everywhere in the universe, whatever beings live in the sky,

upg7:6.3.verse: (may they be) free from oppression, free from hatred, free from suffering, and free from danger.

upg7:7.1.verse: I have attained what is wholesome, by the power of this, may all beings,

upg7:7.2.verse: having understood the King of the True Dhamma’s Doctrine, be led to happiness,

upg7:7.4.verse: be without grief, without continuing despair, (and attain) the supreme happiness of Emancipation.

upg7:8.1.verse: May the True Dhamma last long, may all beings have respect for the Dhamma,

upg7:8.2.verse: may the (rain)-gods rain down at the right time.

upg7:9.1.verse: Just like the Good Kings of old gave protection, likewise

upg7:9.2.verse: may the (present) King protect the people righteously like (he protects) himself.

upg7:10.1.verse: By this practice in conformity with the Dhamma I worship the Buddha,

upg7:10.2.verse: by this practice in conformity with the Dhamma I worship the Dhamma,

upg7:10.3.verse: by this practice in conformity with the Dhamma I worship the Saṅgha,

upg7:10.4.verse: by this practice may I be freed from birth, old age, sickness and death.

upg7:11.1.verse: May my merit bring about the destruction of the pollutants.

upg7:12.1.verse: May my merit be a condition for (gaining) Emacipation.

upg7:13.1.verse: I share my portion of merits with all beings,

upg7:13.2.verse: may all of them share my portion of merits evenly.

upg8:3.1.1.verse: ‘Sister, since I was born with the Noble Birth I have never purposely deprived a living being of life. By that truth may you and the infant have peace.’
“Ever since I was born in the noble birth, sister, I don’t recall having intentionally taken the life of a living creature. By this truth, may both you and your baby be safe.”

upg8:1.1.verse: ° The water that washed the seat of the one reciting

upg8:1.3.verse: “Reciting it will acomplish safety for the child in the womb,”

upg8:1.4.verse: The Elder Aṅgulimāla was told by the Friend of the World.

upg8:2.1.verse: We will recite that safeguard of great power that lasts for an aeon:

upg9:0.1.verse: The Safeguard about the Factors of Awakening

upg9:2.1.verse: While rolling on through the rounds of birth and death all suffering is destroyed

upg9:2.2.verse: (by) the seven Factors of Awakening, which crush Māra’s army.

upg9:3.1.verse: Having Awakened to these seven they are supremely released from the three worlds,

upg9:3.2.verse: and have gone to (that state where there is) no birth, no ageing, no sickness, no death and which is free from fear.

upg9:4.1.verse: Being endowed with this quality and a collection of countless other qualities

upg9:4.2.verse: it is a medicinal mantra: we will recite those factors of Awakening.

upg9:6.1.verse: The Factors of Awakening are agreed upon as mindfulness, and then investigation of the (nature of) things,

upg9:6.2.verse: And after that the Factors of Awakening of energy, joyful-interest and calm,

upg9:6.3.verse: (Then) the Factors of Awakening of concentration and equanimity: these seven

upg9:6.4.verse: were well-proclaimed by the All-Seeing Sage, when developed and practiced

upg9:6.5.verse: They lead to deep knowledge, Emancipation and Awakening:

upg9:7.1.verse: By this declaration of the truth may you be safe at all times!

upg9:8.1.verse: At one time The Lord, having seen that Moggallāna and Kassapa

upg9:8.2.verse: Were sick and suffering, taught these seven Factors of Awakening,

upg9:8.3.verse: And having rejoiced in them, they were freed from illness in an instant:

upg9:9.1.verse: By this declaration of the truth may you be safe at all times!

upg9:10.1.verse: One day the Dhamma-King was oppressed by sickness,

upg9:10.2.verse: And after the Elder Cunda had recited them with respect,

upg9:10.3.verse: Having rejoiced he rose from that affliction on the spot:

upg9:11.1.verse: By this declaration of the truth may you be safe at all times!

upg9:12.1.verse: These afflictions were abandoned by these three Great Seers,

upg9:12.2.verse: Just as the defilements are destroyed by the path, attained in accordance with nature:

upg9:13.1.verse: By this declaration of the truth may you be safe at all times!

upg10:2.1.verse: While fulfilling the conditions for Awakening he was born as a kind of quail,

upg10:2.2.verse: and through his spiritual power the Great Being avoided the forest-fire.

upg10:2.3.verse: This was spoken by the Lord of the World to the Elder Sāriputta,

upg10:2.4.verse: it has great power for a world-cycle: we will recite that safeguard.

upg10:4.1.verse: There is in the world virtue, truth, purity and empathy,

upg10:4.2.verse: by the truth of that I will make an asseveration of supreme truth.

upg10:5.1.verse: After reflecting on the strength of the Dhamma, and recalling the former Victors,

upg10:5.2.verse: relying on the strength of truth, I made an asseveration of truth:

upg10:6.1.verse: “There are wings which fly not, there are feet which walk not,

upg10:6.2.verse: Mother and Father have gone out, Fire, please depart!”

upg10:7.1.verse: This (asseveration) was made by me with truth, and the great blazing fire

upg10:7.2.verse: avoided (this area for) sixteen measures, like fire after reaching water,

upg10:7.3.verse: there is no one my equal for truth, such is my perfection of truth!

upg10:8.1.verse: By this declaration of the truth may you be safe at all times!

upg11:1.1.verse: Thus the tree and the lord, and the lord and the tree

upg11:1.2.verse: With each other quarrel, and each other destroy.

upg11:2.1.verse: So it is with men, wherever a quarrel starts,

upg11:2.2.verse: They dance the peacock dance, like the lord and the tree.

upg11:3.1.verse: I say this to you, hearken, all assembled here,

upg11:3.2.verse: Be friendly, don't quarrel, be not like lord and tree,

upg11:4.1.verse: Train in peace, this is praised by the Awakened Ones,

upg11:4.2.verse: Delight in peace, righteousness, safety will not be destroyed.

upg12:0.1.verse: Verses about a Lion of a Man

upg12:1.1.verse: Having beautiful feet marked with a fine wheel,

upg12:1.2.verse: his long heels are a characteristic mark,

upg12:1.3.verse: his feet decorated with chowrie and sunshade,

upg12:1.4.verse: that indeed is your father, a lion of a man.

upg12:2.1.verse: An excellent and graceful Sakyan prince,

upg12:2.2.verse: with a body full of characteristic marks,

upg12:2.3.verse: a hero who has come for the world’s benefit,

upg12:2.4.verse: that indeed is your father, a lion of a man.

upg12:3.1.verse: Just like the full moon is his beautiful face,

upg12:3.2.verse: dear to gods and men, a Nāga amongst men,

upg12:3.3.verse: walking like a charming lord of elephants,

upg12:3.4.verse: that indeed is your father, a lion of a man.

upg12:4.1.verse: Born into a leading noble family,

upg12:4.2.verse: gods and men revere his feet,

upg12:4.3.verse: having virtue and concentration established in his mind,

upg12:4.4.verse: that indeed is your father, a lion of a man.

upg12:5.1.verse: Having a long, prominent and well-formed nose,

upg12:5.2.verse: cow-like eyelashes, beautiful deep black eyes,

upg12:5.3.verse: his deep black eyebrows (are just like) Indra’s bow,

upg12:5.4.verse: that indeed is your father, a lion of a man.

upg12:6.1.verse: Having a round, sizeable, and well-formed neck,

upg12:6.2.verse: a lion’s jaw, a body like the king of beasts,

upg12:6.3.verse: beautiful golden skin, of supreme colour,

upg12:6.4.verse: that indeed is your father, a lion of a man.

upg12:7.1.verse: Having a very deep, charming, and sweet voice,

upg12:7.2.verse: with a beautiful tongue, red like vermillion,

upg12:7.3.verse: with twenty by twenty beautiful white teeth,

upg12:7.4.verse: that indeed is your father, a lion of a man.

upg12:8.2.verse: a forehead like a plate of purified gold,

upg12:8.3.verse: and hair between the brows like a pure white star,

upg12:8.4.verse: that indeed is your father, a lion of a man.

upg12:9.1.verse: Like the moon going along the dark night path,

upg12:9.2.verse: surrounded by a body of stars,

upg12:9.3.verse: is the Lord of Ascetics in the midst of his disciples,

upg12:9.4.verse: that indeed is your father, a lion of a man.

upg13:1.1.verse: Taṅhaṅkara, the Great Hero, Medhaṅkara, one of Great Fame,

upg13:1.2.verse: Saraṇaṅkara, the World’s Friend, Dīpaṅkara, Resplendant One.

upg13:2.1.verse: Koṅḍañña, the People’s Leader, Maṅgala, the Foremost of Men,

upg13:2.2.verse: Sumana, Happy and Wise, Revata, Increases Delight.

upg13:3.1.verse: Sobhita, Endowed with Virtue, Anomadassī, Supreme Man,

upg13:3.2.verse: Paduma, the Light of the World, Nārada, the Noble Leader.

upg13:4.1.verse: Padumuttara, the Essential, Sumedha, Highest amongst Men,

upg13:4.2.verse: Sujāta, Highest of All Worlds, Piyadassī, Foremost Person.

upg13:5.2.verse: Siddhattha, Matchless in the World, Tissa, Giver of Full Restraint.

upg13:6.1.verse: Phussa, who gives Awakening, Vipassī the Matchless One,

upg13:6.2.verse: Sikhī, Teacher of Benefit, Vessabhū, who gave Happiness.

upg13:7.2.verse: Kassapa, Endowed with Glory, Gotama, the Noble Sakyan.

upg13:8.1.verse: Through their truth, virtue, and the strength of their patience and friendliness,

upg13:8.2.verse: may these (Buddhas) always protect you with good health and happiness!

upg13:9.1.verse: These are the twenty-eight Buddhas, who fulfilled the ten perfections,

upg13:9.2.verse: Having defeated Māra in battle, they attained to Buddhahood,

upg13:9.3.verse: By this declaration of the truth may you have the blessing of success!
